title: The batch sequence stalls after Start
summary: The tank batch sequence starts, but it never gets past its first step and a sequence alarm appears. Use the sequence inspector and the plant to find the cause, repair it and prove that the batch completes again.
objectives: Use the sequence inspector to find the condition a step is waiting for
Separate a command from the field device's response
Verify a repair with a complete batch
instructions: Start the simulation and press Start, as the operator did.
Open the Sequence tab: note the active step, the transition it waits for and the step timer.
Compare what the program commands with what the plant does in the Process view and the alarms.
Submit the root cause you can prove, apply the repair, then run Check: the batch must complete without a sequence fault.
hints: A step that waits for feedback needs the field device to move. Does the command reach the device?
Watch the tank level while the first step is active.

permissives.name: Tank below the high level switch

transitions.name: Inlet valve left the open position

criteria.title: The batch completes
criteria.onFail: The batch did not reach step 5 (complete) within 40 s.

criteria.title: No sequence fault
criteria.onFail: The sequence monitor recorded a step timeout or a deviation.

troubleshooting.symptom: After Start the batch never gets past step 1 and a sequence alarm appears. The tank level does not change.

diagnosisOptions.label: The inlet valve XV-101 does not move although it is commanded open
The inlet valve opens but its open limit switch never reports it
The high level switch LSH-103 is faulty

repairs.label: Free and service the inlet valve XV-101
Replace the open limit switch of XV-101
Replace the high level switch LSH-103

debrief.rootCause: The inlet valve XV-101 was mechanically stuck closed. The program commanded it open in step 1, but the valve never moved.
evidence: The Sequence tab showed step 1 waiting for InletOpen = TRUE while InletValve was TRUE.
The step timer ran out after 5 s and the step timeout alarm activated.
The tank level did not rise, so no water flowed: the valve itself did not open.
debrief.repair: Free and service the inlet valve, then run a complete batch to verify.
debrief.reasoning: A missing limit switch signal alone would leave the tank filling; a level that does not move proves that the valve did not open although it was commanded.
